addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). 1	# Refactoring backlog
2	
3	A complete, trackable catalogue of refactoring opportunities in the **production**
4	code (tests are a separate later pass). Each entry maps to a
5	[Fowler code smell](https://agilepainrelief.com/glossary/code-smells/).
6	
7	Goal is eventual full cleanup — so the tail is captured too, not just the
8	headline items. Tick items off as they land; a PR can reference an `RF-NN` id.
9	
10	## How this is ranked
11	
12	- **Tier = blast radius** (change amplification): how many files you must touch
13	  today to make one routine change. Headline → High → Medium → Low.
14	- **Correctness-risk items are hoisted** above pure tidiness at the same tier.
15	- Each entry tags the **smell**, a rough **effort** (S / M / L), and lists
16	  **sibling sites** rather than repeating the entry per location.
17	- **Out of scope (already decided, not "missed"):** image lazy-loading, signed-URL
18	  batching, and the deliberate deferral of pagination — see
19	  [ADR 0001](adr/0001-list-performance-attack-image-loading-not-pagination.md) and
20	  [ADR 0002](adr/0002-batch-receipt-signed-urls.md). Where a smell touches one of
21	  those decisions, it is cross-referenced, not re-litigated.
22	
23	## Coding preferences applied
24	
25	- **Guard clauses / early returns are good** — fixes that flatten nesting via early
26	  return are encouraged, never flagged.
27	- **Heterogeneous union return types** (`string | number | object`) are a violation;
28	  a *well-formed* discriminated union (see `validateFile()` below) is the model to
29	  copy.
30	- **`any` is a smell wherever a more precise type exists** — prefer `unknown` +
31	  narrowing, typed rows, typed DTOs. Leave `any` only where the library gives no
32	  usable type, and say so.
33	- **Forced-upstream `T | null`** (provider-imposed nullability) is flagged at low
34	  priority only.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Tier 1 — Headline (highest change amplification)
39	
40	### RF-01 — CSV parsers duplicate the whole parse loop (Template Method gap)
41	- [x] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Conditional Complexity · **Effort:** M · **Done**
42	- **Where:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/AmexParser.ts`,
43	  `EQBankParser.ts`, `PCFinancialParser.ts`, `RBCFinancialParser.ts`,
44	  `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts`, `TDBankParser.ts`, `WealthSimpleParser.ts`
45	- **Evidence:** Every parser's `parse()` repeats the identical skeleton —
46	  `removeBOM()` → `parseCSV()` → locate header → resolve column indices → row
47	  loop → `parseDate()` / `parseAmount()` / `normalizeAmount()` → validate
48	  description → `push()` → collect errors. Compare `AmexParser.ts:10-100` with
49	  `EQBankParser.ts:10-88`: structurally the same, differing only in (a) header
50	  detection, (b) column-name matching, and (c) the `invertSign` flag. `BaseCSVParser`
51	  supplies the *utilities* but never a `parse()` **template**, so each subclass
52	  re-implements the orchestration.
53	- **Fix:** Pull the orchestration into `BaseCSVParser` as a Template Method and let
54	  subclasses override only the parts that actually vary:
55	
56	  ```ts
57	  // BaseCSVParser
58	  parse(csvContent: string): CSVParseResult {
59	    const transactions: ParsedTransaction[] = [];
60	    const errors: string[] = [];
61	    const rows = this.parseCSV(this.removeBOM(csvContent));
62	    if (rows.length < 2) { errors.push('CSV file is empty or has no data rows'); return { transactions, errors }; }
63	
64	    const header = this.findHeaderRow(rows);          // hook
65	    if (!header) { errors.push(this.formatError()); return { transactions, errors }; }
66	
67	    for (let i = header.dataStart; i < rows.length; i++) {
68	      const parsed = this.parseRow(rows[i], header.columns, i, errors); // hook
69	      if (parsed) transactions.push(parsed);
70	    }
71	    return { transactions, errors };
72	  }
73	  protected abstract findHeaderRow(rows: string[][]): HeaderInfo | null;
74	  protected abstract parseRow(row: string[], cols: ColumnIndex, i: number, errors: string[]): ParsedTransaction | null;
75	  ```
76	  This removes ~400 lines of copy-paste and makes a new bank a ~20-line subclass.
77	- **Note:** Keep the per-bank sign conventions intact — see the `invertSign` /
78	  Wealth Simple `type`-column rules in `CLAUDE.md`; this is correctness-sensitive.
79	- **Landed:** `BaseCSVParser.parse()` is now the shared Template Method (BOM →
80	  `parseCSV` → empty-file guard → `resolveLayout()` hook → row loop → single
81	  `try/catch`). Subclasses override only `resolveLayout()` (header/column matching)
82	  and `parseRow()`; the single-amount banks share `finalizeRow()`, which
83	  consolidates the `normalizeAmount` → assignment step. Side effects that fell out
84	  of the consolidation:
85	  - Cleared the **6 production type errors** (`normalizeAmount`'s `number | null`
86	    flowing into `amount: number`) — `finalizeRow` guards the null and returns a
87	    plain `number`. `npm run check` drops 118 → 112 (the RF-01-owned slice of the
88	    [type-check-cleanup PRD](prd-type-check-cleanup.md); the remaining 112 are that
89	    PRD's, so "0 errors" only lands once **both** are done).
90	  - Fixed the **Wealth Simple missing-`try/catch`** inconsistency: WS now runs
91	    through the shared template (with `minimumRowCount = 0` to preserve its
92	    header-only-is-valid behaviour), so all seven parsers are wrapped once.
93	  - Removed all six parser `catch (e: any)` sites (they collapse into the base
94	    `catch (e: unknown)`), partially clearing **RF-08**.
95	  - `normalizeAmount`'s `(amount, invertSign)` signature is unchanged (its direct
96	    `BaseCSVParser.test.ts` cases still pass); **RF-11** (flag → subclass property)
97	    was intentionally left for a follow-up. All 229 parser tests / 1551 unit tests
98	    stay green.
99	
100	### RF-02 — Date-filter glue duplicated across 4 list pages (no shared composable)
101	- [x] **Smell:** Divergent Change / Shotgun Surgery + Duplicated Code · **Effort:** M–L · **Done**
102	- **Where:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `receipts/+page.svelte`,
103	  `transactions/+page.svelte`, `reconciliation/+page.svelte`
104	- **Evidence:** All four pages repeat the same filter *glue*: `tempFilterDateFrom/To`
105	  + `urlDateFrom/To` state, an `$effect` to sync temp→URL, and
106	  `applyFilterValues()` / `clearClientFilters()`. Filter-related identifiers per
107	  page: expenses 28, receipts 15, transactions 15, reconciliation 14. The shared
108	  *logic* (URL scheme + `getValidDate` from `dateValidation`) was partly centralised
109	  in commit `0614aa6`, and there is even a spec for it —
110	  `src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` — **but no `sharedDateFilter.ts`
111	  implementation exists and nothing imports it.** The per-page glue was never
112	  extracted. Adding or changing a filter today means four parallel edits.
113	- **Fix:** Build the missing module the spec already describes — a Svelte 5
114	  rune-based composable (`src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.svelte.ts`) exposing the
115	  date-filter state + `apply` / `clear` / URL-sync, and have all four pages consume
116	  it. The orphaned spec becomes its red test.
117	- **Cross-ref:** ADR 0001 notes filters run client-side over the full in-memory list;
118	  keep that behaviour — this entry is about *where the glue lives*, not pagination.
119	- **Landed:** Extracted the pure glue into `src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.ts`
120	  (not a `.svelte.ts` composable — the repo has no rune/component test harness, and
121	  every page keeps its own `$state`/`$derived`/`$effect`/`goto` wiring; only the
122	  pure, node-testable logic moved). Exports: `readDateFilter`, `matchesDateRange`,
123	  `applyDateFilterParams`, `clearDateFilterParams`, plus `toExclusiveEndBoundary`
124	  (transactions bulk-delete bound) and `defaultMonthStart`/`defaultMonthEnd`
125	  (reconciliation default range). All four pages now delegate; the reconciliation
126	  `getDefaultStartDate/End` locals and the transactions inline dateTo math were
127	  deleted.
128	  - The orphaned `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` (which tested *inline copies*, not any
129	    module) was rewritten into 49 characterization tests bound to the real module.
130	    Their expected values were first validated against the pre-extraction page code
131	    via a throwaway oracle harness (run under UTC/Toronto/UTC±12), which also caught
132	    that the old transactions `new Date(to+'T12:00:00').toISOString()` boundary
133	    drifts a day at extreme timezones — so the extracted helpers use TZ-safe Y/M/D
134	    math and the spec pins the corrected values.
135	  - Behaviour-preserving for the 5 glue functions (proven equivalent to all four
136	    pages, incl. the null-date-kept vs transactions-non-null divergence, collapsed
137	    into one predicate). `npm run check` unchanged at 112; full unit suite green
138	    (1566); ESLint on the four pages *dropped* ~10 (zero introduced). The
139	    `hasActiveDateFilter` helper was dropped as YAGNI — the pages' `hasActiveFilters`
140	    combine page-specific filters and a nested call broke a source-introspection
141	    test for no real gain.
142	
143	### RF-03 — List-page table / row / empty-state markup duplicated across 3 pages
144	- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code · **Effort:** L
145	- **Where:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `receipts/+page.svelte`,
146	  `transactions/+page.svelte`
147	- **Evidence:** The three list pages each hand-roll the same table shell — selection
148	  checkbox column, date / merchant / amount columns, an actions column, and a
149	  near-identical empty-state block. They diverge only in the row's domain column
150	  (category vs card type) and the per-row action. This is the second-largest
151	  duplication source after the parsers.
152	- **Fix:** Extract a shared `<DataTable>` / `<ListRow>` pair (or a single list shell
153	  taking column definitions + a row snippet), so a column or empty-state change is
154	  one edit. *Confidence:* file-level confirmed; exact line ranges to be pinned when
155	  the work starts.
156	
157	---
158	
159	## Tier 2 — High
160	
161	### RF-04 — `findPotentialMatches` vs `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` are a copy-paste pair
162	- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Long Parameter List · **Effort:** M
163	- **Where:** `src/lib/services/ReconciliationService.ts:248` and `:366`
164	- **Evidence:** Two symmetric methods (receipt-centric vs transaction-centric) with
165	  the same 5-param signature and near-identical bodies. A change to matching logic
166	  must be mirrored in both.
167	- **Fix:** Unify into one direction-parameterised matcher, or extract the shared
168	  scoring predicate both call. Pairs with RF-06 (the tolerance params).
169	
170	### RF-05 — Long methods in the service layer
171	- [ ] **Smell:** Long Method · **Effort:** M each
172	- **Where & sizes (verified):**
173	  - `PDFExportService.generateReceiptPDF` — `175–404` (~230 lines): builds summary
174	    page, loops categories, draws text/images/tables inline. Extract
175	    `drawSummaryPage()` / `drawCategoryPage()` / `drawReceiptDetails()` / `drawTable()`.
176	  - `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate` — `173–324` (~150): validate → upload → OCR →
177	    persist in one method. Extract per responsibility (see `feedback_ocr_resilience`
178	    — keep the no-orphan-file guarantee).
179	  - `ReceiptService.splitReceipt` — `364–492` (~128).
180	  - `ReconciliationService.reconcile` — `37–152` (~115) and `performMatching` —
181	    `153–247` (~94): nested receipt→transaction loops building three result lists.
182	  - `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — `67–163` (~96).
183	- **Fix:** Extract sub-steps with intention-revealing names; favour guard clauses on
184	  the validation paths.
185	
186	### RF-06 — Matching tolerances are a Long Parameter List / Data Clump
187	- [ ] **Smell:** Long Parameter List + Data Clump · **Effort:** S · *(correctness-adjacent — hoisted)*
188	- **Where:** `ReconciliationService.ts` — `performMatching` (`153`),
189	  `findPotentialMatches` (`248`), `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` (`366`)
190	- **Evidence:** `maxDaysDifference`, `amountTolerance`,
191	  `foreignCurrencyTolerancePercent` travel together through every signature and call
192	  site, with defaults (`?? 3`, `?? 0.01`, `?? 0.05`) scattered inline.
193	- **Fix:** Introduce a `MatchingTolerances` value object with the defaults defined
194	  once, threaded as a single param. Removes the clump and the magic numbers (RF-13)
195	  in one move, and shrinks RF-04's signatures.
196	
197	### RF-07 — Singleton vs dependency-injection split across services
198	- [ ] **Smell:** Inappropriate Static + inconsistency · **Effort:** M
199	- **Where:** Singletons via `static get()`: `ReceiptService.ts:18`,
200	  `TransactionService.ts:20`, `ReconciliationService.ts:28`. DI via constructor:
201	  `ExpenseService` (`constructor(supabase)`, `new`-ed in `CategoryDropdown.svelte:94,295`),
202	  `CategoryService`.
203	- **Evidence:** Two opposite construction patterns for peer services. The singletons
204	  reach for a module-level Supabase client (harder to mock); the DI ones take it as a
205	  param. Tests and callers must know which is which.
206	- **Fix:** Pick one — DI is the more testable target (it already works for
207	  `ExpenseService` / `CategoryService`). Migrate the three singletons to constructor
208	  injection, or document a deliberate rule if the split is intentional.
209	
210	---
211	
212	## Tier 3 — Medium
213	
214	### RF-08 — `any` where a precise type exists
215	- [ ] **Smell:** weak typing (`any`) · **Effort:** S
216	- **Where (10 production sites):** `catch (e: any)` in all CSV parsers
217	  (`AmexParser.ts:95`, `EQBankParser.ts:83`, `PCFinancialParser.ts:75`,
218	  `RBCFinancialParser.ts:96`, `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts:100`, `TDBankParser.ts:83`)
219	  and `TransactionService.ts:176,236`; `ExpenseService.ts:124`
220	  `(receipt: any)`; `CategoryService.ts:283` `updateData: any`.
221	- **Fix:** `catch (e: unknown)` + narrowing; a typed Supabase row interface for the
222	  `map` callback; a typed update DTO for `updateData`. Leave `any` only if the
223	  library gives no usable type — and annotate why at that site.
224	- **Anchor (do this, don't smell):** `ReceiptService.validateFile():158` already
225	  returns `{ ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string }` — the discriminated-union
226	  style to copy, not a smell.
227	
228	### RF-09 — Three inconsistent ways to resolve a row's Category
229	- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code / inconsistency + mild Feature Envy · **Effort:** S
230	- **Where:** `expenses/+page.svelte:1333` rebuilds a `Category` inline from
231	  `category_id` / `category_name` / `category_color`; `expenses/+page.svelte:1379`
232	  uses `categories.find(...)`; `receipts/+page.svelte:1084` and
233	  `reconciliation/+page.svelte:794` use a precomputed `categoryMap`.
234	- **Evidence:** Same conceptual operation ("get the `Category` for this row"), three
235	  implementations. The inline rebuild also hard-codes a fallback colour.
236	- **Fix:** One `resolveCategory(row, categories)` helper, or nest a
237	  `category: Category | null` on the row model so no reconstruction is needed.
238	  Pairs with the Money/Date value-object discussion (Deferred).
239	
240	### RF-10 — `ReconciliationService` does UI display massaging
241	- [ ] **Smell:** Feature Envy · **Effort:** M
242	- **Where:** `convertToDisplayRows` (`:500`) and `sortDisplayRows` (`:571`)
243	- **Evidence:** The service transforms domain `ReconciliationResult` into
244	  UI-oriented display rows and sorts them — presentation concerns leaking into the
245	  service layer.
246	- **Fix:** Move row-shaping + sort to a presenter/component layer; keep the service
247	  returning domain results.
248	
249	### RF-11 — `normalizeAmount(invertSign: boolean)` flag argument
250	- [ ] **Smell:** Flag / Boolean Argument · **Effort:** S

# Refactoring backlog

A complete, trackable catalogue of refactoring opportunities in the **production**
code (tests are a separate later pass). Each entry maps to a
[Fowler code smell](https://agilepainrelief.com/glossary/code-smells/).

Goal is eventual full cleanup — so the tail is captured too, not just the
headline items. Tick items off as they land; a PR can reference an `RF-NN` id.

## How this is ranked

- **Tier = blast radius** (change amplification): how many files you must touch
  today to make one routine change. Headline → High → Medium → Low.
- **Correctness-risk items are hoisted** above pure tidiness at the same tier.
- Each entry tags the **smell**, a rough **effort** (S / M / L), and lists
  **sibling sites** rather than repeating the entry per location.
- **Out of scope (already decided, not "missed"):** image lazy-loading, signed-URL
  batching, and the deliberate deferral of pagination — see
  [ADR 0001](adr/0001-list-performance-attack-image-loading-not-pagination.md) and
  [ADR 0002](adr/0002-batch-receipt-signed-urls.md). Where a smell touches one of
  those decisions, it is cross-referenced, not re-litigated.

## Coding preferences applied

- **Guard clauses / early returns are good** — fixes that flatten nesting via early
  return are encouraged, never flagged.
- **Heterogeneous union return types** (`string | number | object`) are a violation;
  a *well-formed* discriminated union (see `validateFile()` below) is the model to
  copy.
- **`any` is a smell wherever a more precise type exists** — prefer `unknown` +
  narrowing, typed rows, typed DTOs. Leave `any` only where the library gives no
  usable type, and say so.
- **Forced-upstream `T | null`** (provider-imposed nullability) is flagged at low
  priority only.

---

## Tier 1 — Headline (highest change amplification)

### RF-01 — CSV parsers duplicate the whole parse loop (Template Method gap)
- [x] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Conditional Complexity · **Effort:** M · **Done**
- **Where:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/AmexParser.ts`,
  `EQBankParser.ts`, `PCFinancialParser.ts`, `RBCFinancialParser.ts`,
  `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts`, `TDBankParser.ts`, `WealthSimpleParser.ts`
- **Evidence:** Every parser's `parse()` repeats the identical skeleton —
  `removeBOM()` → `parseCSV()` → locate header → resolve column indices → row
  loop → `parseDate()` / `parseAmount()` / `normalizeAmount()` → validate
  description → `push()` → collect errors. Compare `AmexParser.ts:10-100` with
  `EQBankParser.ts:10-88`: structurally the same, differing only in (a) header
  detection, (b) column-name matching, and (c) the `invertSign` flag. `BaseCSVParser`
  supplies the *utilities* but never a `parse()` **template**, so each subclass
  re-implements the orchestration.
- **Fix:** Pull the orchestration into `BaseCSVParser` as a Template Method and let
  subclasses override only the parts that actually vary:

  ```ts
  // BaseCSVParser
  parse(csvContent: string): CSVParseResult {
    const transactions: ParsedTransaction[] = [];
    const errors: string[] = [];
    const rows = this.parseCSV(this.removeBOM(csvContent));
    if (rows.length < 2) { errors.push('CSV file is empty or has no data rows'); return { transactions, errors }; }

    const header = this.findHeaderRow(rows);          // hook
    if (!header) { errors.push(this.formatError()); return { transactions, errors }; }

    for (let i = header.dataStart; i < rows.length; i++) {
      const parsed = this.parseRow(rows[i], header.columns, i, errors); // hook
      if (parsed) transactions.push(parsed);
    }
    return { transactions, errors };
  }
  protected abstract findHeaderRow(rows: string[][]): HeaderInfo | null;
  protected abstract parseRow(row: string[], cols: ColumnIndex, i: number, errors: string[]): ParsedTransaction | null;
  ```
  This removes ~400 lines of copy-paste and makes a new bank a ~20-line subclass.
- **Note:** Keep the per-bank sign conventions intact — see the `invertSign` /
  Wealth Simple `type`-column rules in `CLAUDE.md`; this is correctness-sensitive.
- **Landed:** `BaseCSVParser.parse()` is now the shared Template Method (BOM →
  `parseCSV` → empty-file guard → `resolveLayout()` hook → row loop → single
  `try/catch`). Subclasses override only `resolveLayout()` (header/column matching)
  and `parseRow()`; the single-amount banks share `finalizeRow()`, which
  consolidates the `normalizeAmount` → assignment step. Side effects that fell out
  of the consolidation:
  - Cleared the **6 production type errors** (`normalizeAmount`'s `number | null`
    flowing into `amount: number`) — `finalizeRow` guards the null and returns a
    plain `number`. `npm run check` drops 118 → 112 (the RF-01-owned slice of the
    [type-check-cleanup PRD](prd-type-check-cleanup.md); the remaining 112 are that
    PRD's, so "0 errors" only lands once **both** are done).
  - Fixed the **Wealth Simple missing-`try/catch`** inconsistency: WS now runs
    through the shared template (with `minimumRowCount = 0` to preserve its
    header-only-is-valid behaviour), so all seven parsers are wrapped once.
  - Removed all six parser `catch (e: any)` sites (they collapse into the base
    `catch (e: unknown)`), partially clearing **RF-08**.
  - `normalizeAmount`'s `(amount, invertSign)` signature is unchanged (its direct
    `BaseCSVParser.test.ts` cases still pass); **RF-11** (flag → subclass property)
    was intentionally left for a follow-up. All 229 parser tests / 1551 unit tests
    stay green.

### RF-02 — Date-filter glue duplicated across 4 list pages (no shared composable)
- [x] **Smell:** Divergent Change / Shotgun Surgery + Duplicated Code · **Effort:** M–L · **Done**
- **Where:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `receipts/+page.svelte`,
  `transactions/+page.svelte`, `reconciliation/+page.svelte`
- **Evidence:** All four pages repeat the same filter *glue*: `tempFilterDateFrom/To`
  + `urlDateFrom/To` state, an `$effect` to sync temp→URL, and
  `applyFilterValues()` / `clearClientFilters()`. Filter-related identifiers per
  page: expenses 28, receipts 15, transactions 15, reconciliation 14. The shared
  *logic* (URL scheme + `getValidDate` from `dateValidation`) was partly centralised
  in commit `0614aa6`, and there is even a spec for it —
  `src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` — **but no `sharedDateFilter.ts`
  implementation exists and nothing imports it.** The per-page glue was never
  extracted. Adding or changing a filter today means four parallel edits.
- **Fix:** Build the missing module the spec already describes — a Svelte 5
  rune-based composable (`src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.svelte.ts`) exposing the
  date-filter state + `apply` / `clear` / URL-sync, and have all four pages consume
  it. The orphaned spec becomes its red test.
- **Cross-ref:** ADR 0001 notes filters run client-side over the full in-memory list;
  keep that behaviour — this entry is about *where the glue lives*, not pagination.
- **Landed:** Extracted the pure glue into `src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.ts`
  (not a `.svelte.ts` composable — the repo has no rune/component test harness, and
  every page keeps its own `$state`/`$derived`/`$effect`/`goto` wiring; only the
  pure, node-testable logic moved). Exports: `readDateFilter`, `matchesDateRange`,
  `applyDateFilterParams`, `clearDateFilterParams`, plus `toExclusiveEndBoundary`
  (transactions bulk-delete bound) and `defaultMonthStart`/`defaultMonthEnd`
  (reconciliation default range). All four pages now delegate; the reconciliation
  `getDefaultStartDate/End` locals and the transactions inline dateTo math were
  deleted.
  - The orphaned `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` (which tested *inline copies*, not any
    module) was rewritten into 49 characterization tests bound to the real module.
    Their expected values were first validated against the pre-extraction page code
    via a throwaway oracle harness (run under UTC/Toronto/UTC±12), which also caught
    that the old transactions `new Date(to+'T12:00:00').toISOString()` boundary
    drifts a day at extreme timezones — so the extracted helpers use TZ-safe Y/M/D
    math and the spec pins the corrected values.
  - Behaviour-preserving for the 5 glue functions (proven equivalent to all four
    pages, incl. the null-date-kept vs transactions-non-null divergence, collapsed
    into one predicate). `npm run check` unchanged at 112; full unit suite green
    (1566); ESLint on the four pages *dropped* ~10 (zero introduced). The
    `hasActiveDateFilter` helper was dropped as YAGNI — the pages' `hasActiveFilters`
    combine page-specific filters and a nested call broke a source-introspection
    test for no real gain.

### RF-03 — List-page table / row / empty-state markup duplicated across 3 pages
- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code · **Effort:** L
- **Where:** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`, `receipts/+page.svelte`,
  `transactions/+page.svelte`
- **Evidence:** The three list pages each hand-roll the same table shell — selection
  checkbox column, date / merchant / amount columns, an actions column, and a
  near-identical empty-state block. They diverge only in the row's domain column
  (category vs card type) and the per-row action. This is the second-largest
  duplication source after the parsers.
- **Fix:** Extract a shared `<DataTable>` / `<ListRow>` pair (or a single list shell
  taking column definitions + a row snippet), so a column or empty-state change is
  one edit. *Confidence:* file-level confirmed; exact line ranges to be pinned when
  the work starts.

---

## Tier 2 — High

### RF-04 — `findPotentialMatches` vs `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` are a copy-paste pair
- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code + Long Parameter List · **Effort:** M
- **Where:** `src/lib/services/ReconciliationService.ts:248` and `:366`
- **Evidence:** Two symmetric methods (receipt-centric vs transaction-centric) with
  the same 5-param signature and near-identical bodies. A change to matching logic
  must be mirrored in both.
- **Fix:** Unify into one direction-parameterised matcher, or extract the shared
  scoring predicate both call. Pairs with RF-06 (the tolerance params).

### RF-05 — Long methods in the service layer
- [ ] **Smell:** Long Method · **Effort:** M each
- **Where & sizes (verified):**
  - `PDFExportService.generateReceiptPDF` — `175–404` (~230 lines): builds summary
    page, loops categories, draws text/images/tables inline. Extract
    `drawSummaryPage()` / `drawCategoryPage()` / `drawReceiptDetails()` / `drawTable()`.
  - `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate` — `173–324` (~150): validate → upload → OCR →
    persist in one method. Extract per responsibility (see `feedback_ocr_resilience`
    — keep the no-orphan-file guarantee).
  - `ReceiptService.splitReceipt` — `364–492` (~128).
  - `ReconciliationService.reconcile` — `37–152` (~115) and `performMatching` —
    `153–247` (~94): nested receipt→transaction loops building three result lists.
  - `ExpenseService.getExpenses` — `67–163` (~96).
- **Fix:** Extract sub-steps with intention-revealing names; favour guard clauses on
  the validation paths.

### RF-06 — Matching tolerances are a Long Parameter List / Data Clump
- [ ] **Smell:** Long Parameter List + Data Clump · **Effort:** S · *(correctness-adjacent — hoisted)*
- **Where:** `ReconciliationService.ts` — `performMatching` (`153`),
  `findPotentialMatches` (`248`), `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` (`366`)
- **Evidence:** `maxDaysDifference`, `amountTolerance`,
  `foreignCurrencyTolerancePercent` travel together through every signature and call
  site, with defaults (`?? 3`, `?? 0.01`, `?? 0.05`) scattered inline.
- **Fix:** Introduce a `MatchingTolerances` value object with the defaults defined
  once, threaded as a single param. Removes the clump and the magic numbers (RF-13)
  in one move, and shrinks RF-04's signatures.

### RF-07 — Singleton vs dependency-injection split across services
- [ ] **Smell:** Inappropriate Static + inconsistency · **Effort:** M
- **Where:** Singletons via `static get()`: `ReceiptService.ts:18`,
  `TransactionService.ts:20`, `ReconciliationService.ts:28`. DI via constructor:
  `ExpenseService` (`constructor(supabase)`, `new`-ed in `CategoryDropdown.svelte:94,295`),
  `CategoryService`.
- **Evidence:** Two opposite construction patterns for peer services. The singletons
  reach for a module-level Supabase client (harder to mock); the DI ones take it as a
  param. Tests and callers must know which is which.
- **Fix:** Pick one — DI is the more testable target (it already works for
  `ExpenseService` / `CategoryService`). Migrate the three singletons to constructor
  injection, or document a deliberate rule if the split is intentional.

---

## Tier 3 — Medium

### RF-08 — `any` where a precise type exists
- [ ] **Smell:** weak typing (`any`) · **Effort:** S
- **Where (10 production sites):** `catch (e: any)` in all CSV parsers
  (`AmexParser.ts:95`, `EQBankParser.ts:83`, `PCFinancialParser.ts:75`,
  `RBCFinancialParser.ts:96`, `SimpliiFinancialParser.ts:100`, `TDBankParser.ts:83`)
  and `TransactionService.ts:176,236`; `ExpenseService.ts:124`
  `(receipt: any)`; `CategoryService.ts:283` `updateData: any`.
- **Fix:** `catch (e: unknown)` + narrowing; a typed Supabase row interface for the
  `map` callback; a typed update DTO for `updateData`. Leave `any` only if the
  library gives no usable type — and annotate why at that site.
- **Anchor (do this, don't smell):** `ReceiptService.validateFile():158` already
  returns `{ ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string }` — the discriminated-union
  style to copy, not a smell.

### RF-09 — Three inconsistent ways to resolve a row's Category
- [ ] **Smell:** Duplicated Code / inconsistency + mild Feature Envy · **Effort:** S
- **Where:** `expenses/+page.svelte:1333` rebuilds a `Category` inline from
  `category_id` / `category_name` / `category_color`; `expenses/+page.svelte:1379`
  uses `categories.find(...)`; `receipts/+page.svelte:1084` and
  `reconciliation/+page.svelte:794` use a precomputed `categoryMap`.
- **Evidence:** Same conceptual operation ("get the `Category` for this row"), three
  implementations. The inline rebuild also hard-codes a fallback colour.
- **Fix:** One `resolveCategory(row, categories)` helper, or nest a
  `category: Category | null` on the row model so no reconstruction is needed.
  Pairs with the Money/Date value-object discussion (Deferred).

### RF-10 — `ReconciliationService` does UI display massaging
- [ ] **Smell:** Feature Envy · **Effort:** M
- **Where:** `convertToDisplayRows` (`:500`) and `sortDisplayRows` (`:571`)
- **Evidence:** The service transforms domain `ReconciliationResult` into
  UI-oriented display rows and sorts them — presentation concerns leaking into the
  service layer.
- **Fix:** Move row-shaping + sort to a presenter/component layer; keep the service
  returning domain results.

### RF-11 — `normalizeAmount(invertSign: boolean)` flag argument
- [ ] **Smell:** Flag / Boolean Argument · **Effort:** S
- **Where:** `BaseCSVParser.ts:234`
- **Evidence:** A boolean that switches behaviour, set differently per bank
  (`true` for Amex, `false` for the rest). Well-documented, so low harm — but it is
  the canonical flag-argument shape.
- **Fix:** Once RF-01's Template Method lands, expose sign convention as a subclass
  property/override (e.g. `protected expensesArePositive = false`) rather than a
  call-site boolean. Low priority; do it *with* RF-01, not separately.

---

## Tier 4 — Low

### RF-12 — Magic-number matching defaults
- [ ] **Smell:** Primitive Obsession (magic numbers) · **Effort:** S
- **Where:** `ReconciliationService.ts` — `?? 3`, `?? 0.01`, `?? 0.05` inline.
- **Fix:** Named constants — folds into RF-06's value object. Listed separately only
  so it can be ticked if RF-06 is deferred.

### RF-13 — `PDFExportService.shouldEnablePDFExport` static + state object
- [ ] **Smell:** Inappropriate Static · **Effort:** S
- **Where:** `PDFExportService.ts:159`
- **Evidence:** A `static` predicate taking a 4-field `state` object — reads like UI
  state logic parked on the service. Minor.
- **Fix:** Move to the component/derived-state layer, or leave if it is genuinely
  shared pure logic. Lowest priority.

---

## Deferred — needs a decision before doing

These are real (Primitive Obsession / Data Clump) but the fix is **whole-codebase
shotgun surgery**, so they are parked for an explicit decision rather than scheduled.

### RF-D1 — `Money` value object (amount + currency + exchange rate)
- **Smell:** Primitive Obsession + Data Clump
- **Where:** `total_amount` / `currency` / `exchange_rate_to_cad` travel as a loose
  trio through the `Receipt` model, the reconciliation foreign-currency path, and the
  `formatCurrencyWithEstimate` call sites on expenses / reconciliation.
- **Trade-off:** A `Money` type is the textbook fix and would localise sign/rounding
  risk — **but introducing it touches every parser, service, and page**. For a family
  expense app that may be over-engineering. **Decision needed:** adopt `Money`, or
  consciously keep bare `number` + `currency` and accept the clump.

### RF-D2 — Typed date value object (vs ISO strings everywhere)
- **Smell:** Primitive Obsession
- **Where:** Dates flow as `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings throughout; `toDate()` /
  `toISODateString()` / `getValidDate()` convert at the edges.
- **Trade-off:** The string convention is currently load-bearing and guarded by
  `CLAUDE.md`'s "never `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')`" rule. A value object would add type
  safety but ripples everywhere and risks reintroducing timezone bugs if done
  carelessly. **Decision needed:** introduce a `LocalDate` wrapper, or keep the
  string + helper convention as-is.

---

## Not yet catalogued

- **Test suites** (the large `*.spec.ts` files) — a separate later pass, by
  agreement. Likely findings: duplicated arrange blocks, missing shared fixtures /
  builders, oversized spec files.

content.text:
Short answer: **No — RF-03 is poorly covered, and worse, the coverage that exists works *against* the refactor rather than protecting it.** Here's what I found.

## What actually "tests" these three pages

There is no rendering/behavioral test harness for the pages. Two things exist:

1. **Source-introspection unit tests** (`src/lib/tests/*.spec.ts`) that `readFileSync` the `.svelte` file and assert on its *text* (`content.includes('<table')`, `content.includes('>Category<')`, `content.includes('No expenses found')`, etc.). These never render anything.
2. **Playwright specs** — but the only two that run under `testDir: 'e2e'` are `demo.test.ts` (h1 visible) and `date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts`. The seeded ones in `tests/` (`bulk-receipt-operations`, `receipt-edit-modal`) aren't in the configured `testDir` at all, and per the seam-only testing note there's no auth/seed harness, so they can't execute against real rows anyway.

## Coverage is lopsided across the three RF-03 pages

| Page | Table/row/empty-state coverage |
|---|---|
| `expenses/+page.svelte` | ~25 introspection assertions, many pinned to the **exact markup RF-03 moves** |
| `receipts/+page.svelte` | Introspection tests cover category wiring / duplicate filter / upload — **not** the table shell, columns, or empty-state |
| `transactions/+page.svelte` | **Zero** — only `auth-route-guard` (redirect check) and `sharedDateFilter` reference the file |

So the one page with the most "tests" is the brittle one, and the other two pages RF-03 spans have essentially no safety net for this markup.

## The double failure mode

**(a) They won't catch the real regressions.** A `<DataTable>`/`<ListRow>` extraction risks: columns in the wrong order, the empty-state bound to the wrong predicate, a per-row action wired to the wrong row, the domain column (category vs card type) swapped, selection not propagating. *None* of that is behavior a text-`includes` test can see, and there's no `render()` harness (`@testing-library/svelte` / vitest-browser aren't in the project) to catch it.

**(b) They'll go red on a *correct* refactor.** The expenses assertions are anchored to markup living in `expenses/+page.svelte` — `<table>/<thead>/<tbody>` (`expenses-page.spec.ts:147`), `>Category<` (`:226`), `>Receipt<` (`:237`), `No expenses found` (`:325`), `overflow-x-auto` (`:337`), `type="checkbox"` + `{#each sortedExpenses` (`:352`). The moment RF-03 hoists that markup into a shared component, those strings leave the page file and ~a dozen tests fail with behavior unchanged. The suite punishes the extraction without protecting it.

## What RF-03 needs before it's safe

- **Add a component-render harness** and test the extracted `<DataTable>`/`<ListRow>` directly (columns rendered, empty-state condition, row-action wiring, domain-column slot). This is the missing net, and it's the kind of test that *survives* the markup moving.
- Alternatively/additionally, one thin **Playwright seam per page** proving each page is wired to the shared component — but that's blocked on the auth/seed harness that doesn't exist yet.
- **Repoint or rewrite the expenses introspection tests** to assert against the new component (or as behavioral tests), so they stop encoding "this markup lives in the page file."

Net: the backlog entry rates RF-03 as Effort **L**, and the test situation is the reason — the pre-work isn't the extraction, it's building the behavioral coverage that currently doesn't exist, then un-pinning the expenses tests that would otherwise false-fail.

Want me to draft that `<DataTable>` render-test harness (pick vitest-browser vs @testing-library/svelte first), or spike the extraction on the untested `transactions` page where there are no false-red tests to fight?

# PRD — Playwright seam test for the shared date filter (route-mock harness)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-01
- **Owner:** _unassigned_
- **Related:** [RF-02 (shared date filter)](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-02--date-filter-glue-duplicated-across-4-list-pages-no-shared-composable),
  `src/lib/utils/sharedDateFilter.ts` + its 49-case unit spec.

## 1. Problem

RF-02 extracted the date-filter logic into `sharedDateFilter.ts` and covers its
**correctness** with 49 node-unit tests (validated against the pre-extraction pages
via an oracle harness). What those tests _cannot_ reach is the **wiring** on each
list page — the runes-and-navigation seam that connects the UI controls to that
tested logic:

```
Datepicker → tempFilterDate* ($state) → Apply → applyDateFilterParams → goto
   → URL → readDateFilter ($derived) → matchesDateRange → rendered rows
Clear → clearDateFilterParams → goto → URL cleared → $effect re-syncs temp
```

Today there is **no test that proves this seam is connected**, and the repo has no
harness that could host one:

- `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts` never opens a browser — every case is
  a pure `URLSearchParams` string assertion. It is unit logic in a Playwright
  costume; it now duplicates `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` and proves nothing about the
  UI.
- `e2e/demo.test.ts` only checks the unauthenticated home `<h1>`.
- The `tests/*.spec.ts` Playwright files are orphaned — they sit outside
  `testDir: 'e2e'`, do no auth, and never run.
- There is **no** `globalSetup`, `storageState`, auth fixture, or data seeding. The
  four list pages are auth-gated (`+layout.svelte` guards non-public routes) and
  Supabase-backed, so a page with no session/data renders a login prompt, not a
  filterable list.

The goal is a **thin, reliable Playwright seam test** for the shared date filter,
plus the minimal reusable harness needed to run it — without standing up a backend.

## 2. Scope

### In scope

- A `page.route()` + seeded-session harness that lets a Playwright test load an
  authenticated list page with deterministic, mocked Supabase data — **no live
  backend, no test credentials, no network**.
- **One** seam test on a representative list page (proposal: `/expenses`) proving the
  URL ↔ filtered-DOM ↔ Clear round-trip is wired to `sharedDateFilter`.
- Retiring `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts` (its logic now lives in
  `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts`).
- CI wiring so `npm run test:e2e` runs the new test.

### Out of scope

- Re-testing filter **behaviour/boundaries** (inclusive bounds, null-date rows,
  timezone math, validation, param preservation). That is owned by
  `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts` and stays there — Playwright must not duplicate it.
- Standing up a real/seeded Supabase test project (that is the high-cost path this
  PRD deliberately avoids; see §7).
- E2E for any non-date feature; un-orphaning the parked `tests/*.spec.ts`. The
  harness this PRD builds _enables_ those later, but they are not in scope here.
- Driving the flowbite `<Datepicker>` calendar widget (see §8 / §7).

## 3. Goals / Non-goals

**Goals**

- Prove, in a real browser, that each shared-filter function is actually attached to
  what the user sees — the piece unit tests structurally can't cover.
- Keep the test **thin and stable**: one page, one round-trip, deterministic
  fixtures, no flake.
- Leave behind a small, reusable `e2e/support/` harness (mock session + Supabase
  route stubs) that future seam tests can import.

**Non-goals**

- No boundary/edge coverage in Playwright (unit-owned).
- No assertion of backend or RLS behaviour — the mock returns fixed rows; correctness
  of the query is not under test here.
- No broad e2e suite. This is the "UI is attached" smoke layer, per the project's
  testing rule (unit owns correctness; Playwright proves wiring).

## 4. Success metrics

| Metric                                                  | Baseline                           | Target                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Real browser tests exercising a list page's date filter | 0                                  | 1 (round-trip on `/expenses`) |
| Fake/browserless e2e specs                              | 1 (`date-filter-url-preservation`) | 0 (retired)                   |
| Reusable authed-page e2e harness                        | none                               | 1 (`e2e/support/`)            |
| Flake rate of the new test (10 local runs)              | —                                  | 0                             |
| Added Playwright coverage of filter **logic**           | —                                  | 0 (stays in unit)             |

## 5. Design

### 5.1 The harness (`e2e/support/`)

Two composable helpers, imported by any authed-page test:

- **`seedSession(page)`** — put a valid-looking Supabase session in `localStorage`
  via `page.addInitScript(...)` **before** navigation, so `+layout.svelte`'s
  `supabase.auth.getSession()` resolves and the route guard passes.
  - The client is `createClient(PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
{ auth: { persistSession: true } })` (`src/lib/supabaseClient.ts`), so the
    storage key is supabase-js's default `sb-<project-ref>-auth-token`, where
    `<project-ref>` is derived from `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`. The helper must compute the
    key from the same env var the build used (see §7 env gotcha).
- **`mockSupabase(page, { receipts, ... })`** — `page.route()` the Supabase calls the
  page makes on load and return fixed JSON. Verified load surface for `/expenses`:

  | Intercept                                              | Purpose                        | Fixture                                     |
  | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
  | `**/auth/v1/user` (and `**/auth/v1/token*` on refresh) | `getSession()`/`getUser()`     | one fake user `{ id }`                      |
  | `**/rest/v1/family_members*`                           | `getDefaultFamilyId()`         | one active default membership → `family_id` |
  | `**/rest/v1/receipts*`                                 | `ExpenseService.getExpenses()` | the seed rows (below)                       |
  | `**/rest/v1/expense_categories*`                       | category join                  | `[]` (uncategorized is fine)                |
  | `**/rest/v1/vendor_category_rules*`                    | auto-categorization            | `[]`                                        |

  The exact endpoint list is confirmed by a one-off **discovery run** (`page.on(
'request')` logging) as step 1 of implementation, so the stubs match reality rather
  than assumption.

### 5.2 The seam test (`e2e/date-filter.seam.spec.ts`)

Fixture: two receipts one month apart, e.g. `2025-01-15` and `2025-02-15`.

1. **URL → DOM (proves `readDateFilter` + `matchesDateRange` + `$derived` render):**
   `seedSession` + `mockSupabase`, then `goto('/expenses?dateFrom=2025-02-01')`.
   Assert the Jan row is absent and the Feb row is present.
2. **Clear → reset (proves `clearDateFilterParams` + `goto` + `$effect` re-sync):**
   click **Clear filters**. Assert the URL loses `dateFrom`/`dateTo` and both rows
   render again.
3. **(Stretch) DOM → URL (proves `tempFilter*` + `applyDateFilterParams` + Apply):**
   set the date input and click **Apply**; assert the URL gains `?dateFrom=…`. Gated
   on the flowbite `<Datepicker>` being drivable (see §7); if fiddly, this direction
   is deferred and tracked, not forced.

This is deliberately a single spec, ≤ ~40 lines, asserting _attachment_ only —
concrete filtering rules remain the unit spec's job.

### 5.3 Retire the fake e2e

Delete `e2e/date-filter-url-preservation.spec.ts`. Its intent (pathname-preserving
URL construction) is covered by `applyDateFilterParams`/`clearDateFilterParams` unit
tests plus the new seam's URL assertions.

### 5.4 Representative-page rationale

RF-02 routed all four pages through the same module with identical wiring, so one
page's round-trip proves the pattern. Optional follow-up: a one-line
`goto('/receipts?dateFrom=…')`-and-assert smoke on the other three. If added, `log`
what is and isn't covered so "e2e passes" isn't read as full-UI coverage.

## 6. Sequencing

1. **Discovery run** — log the network + `localStorage` a real `/expenses` load makes;
   pin the exact intercepts and the session-token shape. (Timeboxed; output is the
   fixture list.)
2. **Harness** — `seedSession` + `mockSupabase` in `e2e/support/`, proven by getting
   `/expenses` to render a mocked list at all.
3. **Seam test** — steps 1–2 (round-trip); add step 3 if the Datepicker is drivable.
4. **Retire** the fake spec; ensure `npm run test:e2e` is green in CI (`webServer`
   already builds+previews; add a dummy `.env` with `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/anon key).
5. **(Optional)** URL smoke on the other three pages.

Each step is independently reviewable; stop after 3 if the optional smoke isn't wanted.

## 7. Risks & mitigations

- **Env at build time.** `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are
  `$env/static/public` and must exist for `npm run build` in the `webServer`. Provide
  dummy values in CI; the harness derives the `localStorage` key from the same URL so
  the seeded session matches. _Mitigation:_ a committed `.env.e2e` (dummy values) and
  a short note in the test README.
- **Mock drift / coupling to supabase-js internals.** The auth token endpoints and
  storage-key format are supabase-js implementation details; a client upgrade could
  shift them. _Mitigation:_ keep the discovery script in `e2e/support/` to re-pin
  quickly; assert on user-visible outcomes (rows, URL), not on request internals.
- **flowbite `<Datepicker>` is awkward to drive** (calendar popover; it also doesn't
  forward `id`). _Mitigation:_ make the URL→DOM→Clear round-trip the primary,
  Datepicker-free proof; treat the Apply-via-picker direction as stretch.
- **Slower/heavier than unit** (`build && preview` + browser). _Mitigation:_ exactly
  one spec; `fullyParallel:false` and single worker already configured.
- **Scope creep into logic testing.** Reviewers should reject any boundary/edge
  assertions here — they belong in `sharedDateFilter.spec.ts`.

## 8. Open questions

- **Representative page:** `/expenses` (richest load surface, good exercise of the
  harness) vs `/transactions` (also has the `toExclusiveEndBoundary` bulk-delete
  path). Recommend `/expenses` for the seam; leave transactions' delete path to unit.
- **Stretch Apply-direction:** worth the flowbite `<Datepicker>` interaction cost, or
  is the URL→DOM→Clear round-trip a sufficient seam proof on its own?
- **Harness location/naming:** `e2e/support/` here; align with wherever the parked
  `tests/*.spec.ts` will eventually move if we un-orphan them.
- **Other three pages:** add the one-line URL smoke now, or defer until a second
  page's wiring diverges?

</context>

Not quite — there are two corrections, and the second one flips the cost calculus in favour of the option you're calling "less benefit."

## Correction 1: the PRD isn't about RF-03

`prd-e2e-date-filter-seam.md` builds a seam test for the **date filter** (RF-02's wiring): `Datepicker → $state → Apply → goto → URL → readDateFilter → matchesDateRange → rows`. It says nothing about the table/row/empty-state markup that RF-03 moves. So "do the PRD" does **not** cover RF-03.

What makes the PRD *relevant* to RF-03 is a side effect: the reusable `seedSession` + `mockSupabase` harness it leaves behind in `e2e/support/`. That harness is what would later let you write a *page-level* seam test for RF-03 ("load `/expenses` with mocked rows, confirm the extracted `<DataTable>` still renders them"). The PRD's date-filter test is the first customer of that harness, not the RF-03 coverage itself.

## Correction 2: they're different layers, and the component path is the *cheaper* one here

I wouldn't call component tests "less benefit" — and the reason is concrete: **the component-render harness already exists and is wired, with zero tests using it.**

`vite.config.ts` has a `client` project: `environment: 'browser'`, `provider: 'playwright'`, `include: ['src/**/*.svelte.{test,spec}.{js,ts}']`, `setupFiles: ['./vitest-setup-client.ts']` — and `vitest-browser-svelte` + `@vitest/browser` are already in `package.json`. So a `src/lib/components/DataTable.svelte.spec.ts` doing `render(DataTable, { props })` Just Works under `npm run test:unit` today. No new deps, no discovery run, no supabase-internals coupling.

So the real comparison for RF-03 is:

| | Component tests (`<DataTable>`) | PRD seam harness (mock+route) |
|---|---|---|
| **Harness cost** | **Already built, 0 tests use it** | Net-new: `seedSession`, `mockSupabase`, discovery run, env wiring |
| **What it pins** | Columns/order, empty-state condition, row snippet, selection, domain-column slot — *exactly what an extraction risks* | Page↔data↔URL wiring in a real browser |
| **Coupling risk** | Low (pure props) | Couples to supabase-js token/storage internals (flagged in PRD §7) |
| **What it can't prove** | That each *page* passes the right column-defs/rows in | The component's internal column matrix (deliberately out of scope) |

They're **complementary, not substitutes**. Component tests own the extracted component's correctness (cheap, now); a thin per-page seam (via the PRD harness) later proves each page is wired to it. For RF-03 specifically, the component tests are the *primary, higher-value, lower-cost* net — the opposite of "less benefit."

## So the accurate framing

It's not "PRD **or** component tests" as two routes to the same goal. It's:

- **RF-03 safety → component tests**, because the harness is already there and they pin what the extraction risks. Plus repoint the ~dozen brittle expenses introspection assertions (`<table`, `>Category<`, `No expenses found`, `overflow-x-auto`, `{#each sortedExpenses`) at the new component. This is the path I'd take first.
- **The PRD → a separate track** that proves the *date-filter* wiring and, as a bonus, leaves the authed-page mock harness that a future *optional* RF-03 per-page seam smoke could reuse.

If you only do one thing before RF-03, do the component tests — they're nearly free here and directly protect the refactor. The PRD is worth doing on its own merits (the date-filter seam is genuinely untested), but don't do it *as* RF-03 coverage.

# Test-Driven Development

## Philosophy

**Core principle**: Tests should verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't.

**Good tests** are integration-style: they exercise real code paths through public APIs. They describe _what_ the system does, not _how_ it does it. A good test reads like a specification - "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists. These tests survive refactors because they don't care about internal structure.

**Bad tests** are coupled to implementation. They mock internal collaborators, test private methods, or verify through external means (like querying a database directly instead of using the interface). The warning sign: your test breaks when you refactor, but behavior hasn't changed. If you rename an internal function and tests fail, those tests were testing implementation, not behavior.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Anti-Pattern: Horizontal Slices

**DO NOT write all tests first, then all implementation.** This is "horizontal slicing" - treating RED as "write all tests" and GREEN as "write all code."

This produces **crap tests**:

- Tests written in bulk test _imagined_ behavior, not _actual_ behavior
- You end up testing the _shape_ of things (data structures, function signatures) rather than user-facing behavior
- Tests become insensitive to real changes - they pass when behavior breaks, fail when behavior is fine
- You outrun your headlights, committing to test structure before understanding the implementation

**Correct approach**: Vertical slices via tracer bullets. One test → one implementation → repeat. Each test responds to what you learned from the previous cycle. Because you just wrote the code, you know exactly what behavior matters and how to verify it.

```
WRONG (horizontal):
  RED:   test1, test2, test3, test4, test5
  GREEN: impl1, impl2, impl3, impl4, impl5

RIGHT (vertical):
  RED→GREEN: test1→impl1
  RED→GREEN: test2→impl2
  RED→GREEN: test3→impl3
  ...
```

## Workflow

### 1. Planning

When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so that test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Before writing any code:

- [ ] Confirm with user what interface changes are needed
- [ ] Confirm with user which behaviors to test (prioritize)
- [ ] Identify opportunities for deep modules (small interface, deep implementation) — run the `/codebase-design` skill for the vocabulary and the testability checks
- [ ] List the behaviors to test (not implementation steps)
- [ ] Get user approval on the plan

Ask: "What should the public interface look like? Which behaviors are most important to test?"

**You can't test everything.** Confirm with the user exactly which behaviors matter most. Focus testing effort on critical paths and complex logic, not every possible edge case.

### 2. Tracer Bullet

Write ONE test that confirms ONE thing about the system:

```
RED:   Write test for first behavior → test fails
GREEN: Write minimal code to pass → test passes
```

This is your tracer bullet - proves the path works end-to-end.

### 3. Incremental Loop

For each remaining behavior:

```
RED:   Write next test → fails
GREEN: Minimal code to pass → passes
```

Rules:

- One test at a time
- Only enough code to pass current test
- Don't anticipate future tests
- Keep tests focused on observable behavior

### 4. Refactor

After all tests pass, look for [refactor candidates](refactoring.md):

- [ ] Extract duplication
- [ ] Deepen modules (move complexity behind simple interfaces)
- [ ] Apply SOLID principles where natural
- [ ] Consider what new code reveals about existing code
- [ ] Run tests after each refactor step

**Never refactor while RED.** Get to GREEN first.

## Checklist Per Cycle

```
[ ] Test describes behavior, not implementation
[ ] Test uses public interface only
[ ] Test would survive internal refactor
[ ] Code is minimal for this test
[ ] No speculative features added
```

input.content:
---
name: reference-component-test-harness
description: How to write Svelte component render tests in this repo (browser vitest project + naming gotcha)
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Svelte component **render** tests run in the `client` vitest project
(`environment: 'browser'`, `provider: 'playwright'`, chromium) configured in
`vite.config.ts` under `test.projects`. Use `render` from `vitest-browser-svelte`,
locators from the returned queries (`getByRole`/`getByText`), and retriable
`await expect.element(...).toBeVisible()`.

**Naming gotcha (load-bearing):** the browser project only includes

The tables **diverge more than the backlog's "only category vs card type" claim**: checkbox column (2 of 3), thumbnail rendering (img vs pdf-badge vs none), sort indicators (↑↓ vs none vs ▲▼), row-click-to-modal (2 of 3), conditional row styling, and empty-state count (1 vs 3 vs 2). Base directory for this skill: /Users/marklevison/.claude/skills/codebase-design

# Codebase Design

Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Use this language and these principles wherever code is being designed or restructured. The aim is leverage for callers, locality for maintainers, and testability for everyone.

## Glossary

Use these terms exactly — don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary." Consistent language is the whole point.

**Module** — anything with an interface and an implementation. Deliberately scale-agnostic: a function, class, package, or tier-spanning slice. _Avoid_: unit, component, service.

**Interface** — everything a caller must know to use the module correctly: the type signature, but also invariants, ordering constraints, error modes, required configuration, and performance characteristics. _Avoid_: API, signature (too narrow — they refer only to the type-level surface).

**Implementation** — what's inside a module, its body of code. Distinct from **Adapter**: a thing can be a small adapter with a large implementation (a Postgres repo) or a large adapter with a small implementation (an in-memory fake). Reach for "adapter" when the seam is the topic; "implementation" otherwise.

**Depth** — leverage at the interface: the amount of behaviour a caller (or test) can exercise per unit of interface they have to learn. A module is **deep** when a large amount of behaviour sits behind a small interface, **shallow** when the interface is nearly as complex as the implementation.

**Seam** _(Michael Feathers)_ — a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; the *location* at which a module's interface lives. Where to put the seam is its own design decision, distinct from what goes behind it. _Avoid_: boundary (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

**Adapter** — a concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. Describes *role* (what slot it fills), not substance (what's inside).

**Leverage** — what callers get from depth: more capability per unit of interface they learn. One implementation pays back across N call sites and M tests.

**Locality** — what maintainers get from depth: change, bugs, knowledge, and verification concentrate in one place rather than spreading across callers. Fix once, fixed everywhere.

## Deep vs shallow

**Deep module** = small interface + lots of implementation:

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Small Interface   │  ← Few methods, simple params
├─────────────────────┤
│                     │
│  Deep Implementation│  ← Complex logic hidden
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

**Shallow module** = large interface + little implementation (avoid):

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│       Large Interface           │  ← Many methods, complex params
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│  Thin Implementation            │  ← Just passes through
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

When designing an interface, ask:

- Can I reduce the number of methods?
- Can I simplify the parameters?
- Can I hide more complexity inside?

## Principles

- **Depth is a property of the interface, not the implementation.** A deep module can be internally composed of small, mockable, swappable parts — they just aren't part of the interface. A module can have **internal seams** (private to its implementation, used by its own tests) as well as the **external seam** at its interface.
- **The deletion test.** Imagine deleting the module. If complexity vanishes, it was a pass-through. If complexity reappears across N callers, it was earning its keep.
- **The interface is the test surface.** Callers and tests cross the same seam. If you want to test *past* the interface, the module is probably the wrong shape.
- **One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.** Don't introduce a seam unless something actually varies across it.

## Designing for testability

Good interfaces make testing natural:

1. **Accept dependencies, don't create them.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function processOrder(order, paymentGateway) {}

   // Hard to test
   function processOrder(order) {
     const gateway = new StripeGateway();
   }
   ```

2. **Return results, don't produce side effects.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function calculateDiscount(cart): Discount {}

   // Hard to test
   function applyDiscount(cart): void {
     cart.total -= discount;
   }
   ```

3. **Small surface area.** Fewer methods = fewer tests needed. Fewer params = simpler test setup.

## Relationships

- A **Module** has exactly one **Interface** (the surface it presents to callers and tests).
- **Depth** is a property of a **Module**, measured against its **Interface**.
- A **Seam** is where a **Module**'s **Interface** lives.
- An **Adapter** sits at a **Seam** and satisfies the **Interface**.
- **Depth** produces **Leverage** for callers and **Locality** for maintainers.

## Rejected framings

- **Depth as ratio of implementation-lines to interface-lines** (Ousterhout): rewards padding the implementation. We use depth-as-leverage instead.
- **"Interface" as the TypeScript `interface` keyword or a class's public methods**: too narrow — interface here includes every fact a caller must know.
- **"Boundary"**: overloaded with DDD's bounded context. Say **seam** or **interface**.

## Going deeper

- **Deepening a cluster given its dependencies** — see [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md): dependency categories, seam discipline, and replace-don't-layer testing.
- **Exploring alternative interfaces** — see [DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md](DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md): spin up parallel sub-agents to design the interface several radically different ways, then compare on depth, locality, and seam placement.

Good — with the design vocabulary in hand, here are answers to all three, framed as decisions about the `<DataTable>` **interface** and where the **seam** sits.

## 1. Sortable on any column — yes, and the shell should *own* it

Right now sorting is duplicated glue with three different looks: expenses `↑/↓` with full a11y (`aria-sort`, `role="columnheader"`, `tabindex`), transactions `▲/▼` with none of the a11y, receipts clickable headers with no indicator at all. That's accidental drift.

Make sort part of the `<DataTable>` **interface** via column definitions, and let the shell own the state + one consistent, accessible indicator:

```ts
type Column<Row> = {
  key: string;
  header: string;
  align?: 'left' | 'right';
  sortable?: boolean;                    // opt any column in
  sortValue?: (row: Row) => string | number;  // shell sorts generically
  cell: Snippet<[Row]>;                  // page supplies the cell content
};
```

The shell owns `sortColumn`/`sortDirection`, renders the single indicator with `aria-sort` everywhere, and sorts the rows itself from `sortValue`. That passes the **deletion test**: delete `<DataTable>` and the sort state + indicator + a11y reappear in all three pages. `sortValue` covers every current case cleanly — ISO date strings sort lexically, merchant/vendor by string, amount numerically, card type by string.

## 2. "Is there any action?" — yes, but they differ, so actions are a snippet, not a prop

Factually, per page:
- **Expenses** — *no* action buttons. Last column is the Category dropdown; editing happens via **row-click → modal**.
- **Receipts** — **Delete** button; also **row-click → modal**.
- **Transactions** — **Edit / Exclude / Delete** buttons; **no** row-click.

So there's no fixed action set to bake into the interface. Actions belong in a per-row `cell` snippet (the trailing column) — the shell exposes the slot, the page fills it. Baking `onEdit/onDelete` props in would make the module **shallow** (a big interface that just passes through to three different handlers).

## 3. Could we achieve consistency? — yes for the *accidental* divergence, and we should

This is the key call. Split the divergence into essential (keep as config/snippet) vs accidental (normalize now, so the module is **deep** rather than a flex-everything shell):

| Divergence | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Sort glyph + a11y (↑↓ / ▲▼ / none) | **Accidental** | Standardize on `↑↓` + full `aria-sort`. Pure win. |

Got it. That turns RF-03 from a pure refactor into **refactor + two deliberate features**, applied uniformly:

- **Universal multi-select** with modifier semantics (plain toggle, `Shift` range, `Cmd/Ctrl` additive-toggle) — new behavior, and transactions gains selection.
- **Universal click-to-edit** — every page's row-click opens its editor (transactions moves off its inline Edit button).

## Design: keep the fiddly part a deep module

The modifier/range/anchor logic is pure, fiddly, and doesn't exist anywhere yet — exactly what belongs **behind a small interface**, tested through that interface without a browser:

- **`selectionModel.ts`** (pure, node-tested) — the star. Given the visible row order + current state + a click with modifiers → next `{ selected, anchor }`. This is the correctness-critical new logic; it gets exhaustive fast unit tests (the "unit owns correctness" layer).
- **`<DataTable>`** (component-tested) — a thin adapter that renders columns + sort + the selection column *using* the model. Its tests only prove wiring (checkbox+Shift calls the model, rows render, empty states show).
- **Pages** — supply `columns` (with `cell` snippets for thumbnails/badges/dropdowns/actions), bind `selected`, and pass `onRowClick`.

**Deletion test:** delete these and the sort state, the tri-state select-all, *and* a hand-rolled range-select would reappear in three pages — so they earn their keep.

**Selection semantics I'll implement** (correct me if any differ from what you picture):
- Modifiers live on the **checkbox**; plain **row-click stays = edit**.
- Plain checkbox click → toggle that row, set anchor.
- `Shift`+click → select the contiguous range anchor→row in *current visible order*, union into the selection; anchor unchanged. No anchor (or anchor filtered out after sort) → falls back to plain toggle.
- `Cmd/Ctrl`+click → additive toggle, set anchor.
- Range uses the **sorted/filtered order** the shell is showing, so Shift after a re-sort does the intuitive thing.

Checkpoint — the tested shell is done. Here's where RF-03 stands.

## Landed this turn (all test-first, suite green at 1599)

| Module | Kind | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `selectionModel.ts` | pure (node) | 16 — plain/Shift/Cmd-Ctrl, reverse range, re-sorted order, missing anchor, tri-state select-all |
| `tableSort.ts` | pure (node) | 7 — asc/desc, locale strings, stable ties, no-mutation, toggle rules |
| `DataTable.svelte` | component (browser) | 7 — headers/cells, empty snippet, sort toggle, row-click, interactive-cell guard, checkbox+**Shift range**, select-all |
| `FilteredEmptyState.svelte` | component (earlier) | 3 |

All lint-clean, type-clean, no warnings in touched files. The deep-module decomposition held up: the fiddly correctness (selection + sort) sits in fast node tests; the browser tests only prove wiring.

**Two Svelte-5 gotchas found and recorded** (both were *test* bugs, not component bugs): `getByRole('button',{name})` also matched the `<tr role="button">` via aggregated accessible name (`.first()` clicked the row); and row-open must be **cell-level `onclick`**, because `stopPropagation`/`event.target` guards are unreliable under Svelte 5 event delegation. The interface you shaped — `sortValue` presence = sortable, one accessible indicator, `interactive` cells opt out of row-open — all works.

## Next: migrate the three pages (the large, riskier part)

This is where the behavior changes land and where the brittle introspection tests will need repointing. I'd go **one page per step, suite green between each**:

1. **Expenses** — checkbox + thumbnail + sortable date/merchant/amount + category dropdown (`interactive`) + row-click modal. Repoint the ~dozen introspection assertions (`<table`, `>Category<`, `{#each sortedExpenses`, etc.) to the new structure.
2. **Receipts** — image (pdf/img) + badges + Delete (`interactive`) + needs-review empty state + row-click modal.
3. **Transactions** — **new behavior**: gains selection + Shift/Cmd multi-select, and row-click-to-edit replacing its inline Edit button; amount colour + card badge + Exclude/Delete actions.

Each page migration is a meaningful diff (these files are 660–1400 lines). Want me to proceed with **expenses first** and check in after it's green, or do all three before reporting back?
Are the rendering based tests stable? How do we update them if there is meaningful choice to change something in the ui?

Good questions — they get at the whole reason for preferring these over the `content.includes('<table')` introspection tests. Let me answer both honestly, grounded in what we just built.

## Are they stable?

**Deterministic: yes, no flake seen.** I ran `DataTable.svelte.spec.ts` a dozen-plus times this session; passes were consistent and the failures were all *deterministic* (the locator bug, the delegation issue) — never intermittent. The anti-flake machinery is real:
- Assertions are **retriable** — `expect.element(...).toBeVisible()` / `toHaveTextContent()` poll until true or timeout, and Playwright auto-waits for actionability before clicking. That's why a genuinely-failing assertion took ~10s (it kept retrying) while passes are milliseconds. So failures are *slow*, not *flaky*.

**The honest costs:**
- **Slower + heavier** than node tests (chromium boot ~1–2s; each test tens–hundreds of ms). That's why the pyramid matters — I kept the browser tests to thin *wiring* (7 tests) and put the correctness (16 + 7) in fast node tests. If a browser test is ever slow/quarantined, the correctness net still holds.
- **Slow feedback on a wrong test** — a bad assertion burns the full timeout. Mitigation during dev: drop to native `element.click()` / `container.querySelector` to isolate "handler wired?" from "locator right?" (exactly how I found the two bugs).
- **Infra dependency** — they need the browser; CI must provision chromium.

**The stability that matters most: they survive refactors.** Because they query by **role / visible text / user action**, not markup, you can reorder cells, restyle, swap `<div>`→`<section>` and they stay green. That's the opposite of the introspection tests, which break on any cosmetic move *and* give false confidence. So "stable" in the sense you care about — robust to change — yes, by construction.

## How do we update them on a deliberate UI change?

The key is distinguishing two cases, and the tests are designed so only the second one touches them:

**1. Refactor (same behavior, new markup) → tests should NOT change.** That's the value. Concrete example from what we built: the sort test asserts the **row order** changes (`getByTestId('name').first()` becomes `'Alpha'`), *not* the `↑/↓` glyph. So if you later decide the indicator should be `▲/▼`, the tests stay green — because I asserted the *outcome*, not the decoration. That's the deliberate lever: **assert user-observable outcomes, not incidental details**, and cosmetic changes ripple to nothing.

**2. Behavior change (the UI genuinely does something different) → update test-first.** The test *is* the executable spec, so you change it the same red→green way we've been working:
- Edit the assertion to the new expectation (RED) → edit the component (GREEN).
- Example: rename "Clear all filters" → "Reset". `getByRole('button', { name: 'Clear all filters' })` breaks — *correctly*, because you changed a user-facing/a11y contract. You update that one query. The break is a **precise checklist** of what changed, not noise.
- Because queries are semantic, the edits are localized: a label change touches the one line that names the label, not twenty structural assertions.

**Two amplifiers specific to our setup:**
- **Interface changes go through the fixture.** If `<DataTable>`'s props change (say, a new column option), you edit `DataTableFixture.svelte` once; the seven tests flow through it. Contrast with per-page markup asserted in twenty places.
- **We're *retiring* the brittle tests as we migrate.** Part of the page migration is replacing `content.includes('>Category<')`-style assertions (which break on cosmetic change) with these behavior tests. So the update story gets strictly better as RF-03 lands — fewer false failures, and the ones you do get are meaningful.

**One caution to keep them stable:** don't over-specify. If a cosmetic tweak ever breaks a component test, treat it as a smell that the test asserted a decoration — loosen it to assert the outcome. And no DOM snapshots (I avoided them deliberately — they're introspection-brittle wearing a different hat).

Net: they're stable and refactor-proof by design; a *behavior* change is a deliberate, localized, test-first edit where the failing test tells you exactly which user-facing contract moved. <style>
	/*
	 * #{#exp9a} Criterion 9: Responsive expenses table.
	 *
	 * Horizontal scrolling is applied only on small screens. On desktop the
	 * wrapper stays `overflow: visible` so the in-row category dropdown is not
	 * clipped by an overflow context — see commit "Expense Tab fix Dropdown
	 * Clipping issue", which is why `overflow-x-auto` was removed from the markup.
	 */
	@media (max-width: 640px) {
		.expenses-table {
			overflow-x: auto;
		}
	}
</style>

content.text: Important catch — that CSS documents a deliberate fix: `overflow-x-auto` was **removed** from the expenses table on desktop so the in-row `CategoryDropdown` isn't clipped (it's applied only on mobile via this media query). My `DataTable` wrapper uses `overflow-x-auto` unconditionally, which would **reintroduce the dropdown-clipping bug**. I'll make the shell's overflow responsive (scroll on mobile, visible on desktop) — matching that intent and harmless for the other two tables:
