Svelte component **render** tests run in the `client` vitest project
(`environment: 'browser'`, `provider: 'playwright'`, chromium) configured in
`vite.config.ts` under `test.projects`. Use `render` from `vitest-browser-svelte`,
locators from the returned queries (`getByRole`/`getByText`), and retriable
`await expect.element(...).toBeVisible()`.

**Naming gotcha (load-bearing):** the browser project only includes
`src/**/*.svelte.{test,spec}.{js,ts}`. A render test MUST be named
`Foo.svelte.spec.ts` — a plain `Foo.spec.ts` runs in the Node `server` project
instead, where `render`/DOM aren't available. Most existing `*.spec.ts` files
next to components (e.g. `CategoryDropdown.spec.ts`) are node-side
**source-introspection** tests (`readFileSync` + `content.includes`), not render
tests — don't confuse the two.

First real render test / working example: `src/lib/components/FilteredEmptyState.svelte.spec.ts`.
More involved example (sort/selection wiring via a `*Fixture.svelte` that supplies
snippet props): `DataTable.svelte.spec.ts` + `DataTableFixture.svelte`.
Run a single one with `npx vitest run --project client <path>`. Relates to
[[feedback-testing-pyramid-playwright-seam-only]] — these component tests are the
unit-level net for extracted UI (RF-03), distinct from the Playwright seam layer.

**Two Svelte-5 gotchas that cost real time (both cases where the test lied, not the code):**
1. `getByRole('button', { name })` matches the name as a **substring**, and a
   `<tr role="button">` exposes an accessible name aggregated from its cells
   (e.g. "Beta 20 Act"). So `getByRole('button', { name: 'Act' })` also matches the
   row, and `.first()` clicked the row, not the button. Use `{ exact: true }` or
   scope the query.
2. Row-click-to-open should be wired as **cell-level `onclick`** on each
   non-interactive `<td>`, NOT `<tr onclick>` + `stopPropagation`/`event.target`
   guard. Under Svelte 5 event delegation, `stopPropagation` in a cell doesn't
   reliably stop the row handler and `event.target.closest(...)` guards misfire.
   The pure JS `element.click()` fires handlers even when the vitest-browser locator
   is targeting the wrong element — handy for isolating "is the handler wired?" from
   "is the locator right?".

content.text:
Fixed. Real bug, now covered.

## What was wrong

The selection **state** was correct (that's why the header showed the indeterminate dash), but the row checkboxes didn't *visually* check. Cause: my `onRowCheckbox` called `event.preventDefault()` to keep the box state-driven — but on a controlled `<input type="checkbox">`, `preventDefault` triggers the browser's **canceled-activation**, which reverts `checked` *after* Svelte sets it. Net: state updates, box stays visually unchecked.

My DataTable test missed it because it only asserted the selection **state** (a testid), never the checkbox's visual `checked`.

## The fix (test-first)

1. Added `toBeChecked()` assertions → **reproduced** the bug (`Received element is not checked` while state was right).
2. Fixed the handlers: **don't `preventDefault`** — let the box toggle natively, then force `event.currentTarget.checked` to match state (state wins, since a Shift-range can leave the clicked row's own value unchanged and Svelte's one-way `checked` won't re-assert that case).
3. Hardened the tests to cover the visual state on select, **Shift-range**, **deselect**, and **select-all/none** — `not.toBeChecked()` too.

**Verified:** DataTable 7/7, full suite **1599 green**, build clean. Version 0.24 → 0.25.

shouldn't bulk delete be available to all? Definitely expenses.

Good question — and yes. Right now expenses has selection checkboxes that do **nothing** (the old code even said "UI ready, backend needed"), which is worse than not having them. It should be consistent across all three list pages.

Here's the design, and one thing to confirm before I wire destructive actions:

## What "bulk delete" means per page

| Page | Bulk delete deletes… | Service call |
|---|---|---|
| **Receipts** | the selected receipts (record + stored file) | `ReceiptService.bulkDeleteReceipts(ids)` — **already exists** |
| **Expenses** | the underlying **receipts** (an expense *is* a receipt, 1:1 — computed, not stored) | same `bulkDeleteReceipts(receipt_ids)`, then reload expenses |
| **Transactions** | the selected transactions | `TransactionService` bulk delete (I'll confirm the exact method when I migrate it) |

The important nuance: on **expenses**, "delete" removes the receipt **and its file** (there's no separate expense record). So the confirm dialog must say that plainly, not imply it only removes a categorization. Deletes stay behind a confirmation (they're irreversible — consistent with your no-confirm-for-*reversible*-only rule).

## Recommended approach: extract a shared bar

Receipts already has the whole bulk-action affordance (selected-count text, Delete button, confirm dialog, optimistic update + rollback). Rather than copy it twice, I'd extract a **`<BulkActionBar>`** (count + delete button + confirm) that takes the selection and a page-specific `onDelete` callback — so all three are guaranteed consistent, and it's the same dedupe spirit as the `DataTable` work. Each page keeps only its own delete action (receipts/transactions delete their own rows; expenses deletes the underlying receipts).

## Sequencing

1. Finish the **receipts** `DataTable` migration (keep its existing bulk delete working through the new selection state).
2. **Extract** the bulk-action bar from receipts into the shared component (test-first).
3. Wire **expenses** → bulk-delete underlying receipts (with a clear "removes the receipt + file" confirm).
4. Wire **transactions** → selection + bulk delete during its migration.

**One confirm before I build the destructive parts:** OK with expenses "delete" removing the underlying receipt + file (the only correct meaning, since expenses aren't stored separately)? And do you want the shared `<BulkActionBar>`, or would you rather I keep the bulk-delete inline per page for now?

I'll continue reading/finishing receipts either way — the answer only changes steps 2–4.

**Net −316/+246** on the page (the hand-rolled table + selection/sort machinery gone). Kept everything domain-specific as snippets/config.

content.text:
## Reconciliation: no, not really — and here's why

I checked. Reconciliation shares the *date filter* (already extracted in RF-02) and the generic `overflow-x-auto rounded border` wrapper, but its table is a **fundamentally different shape** than the three flat lists:

- **Grouped two-tier header with `colspan`** — "Receipts" spans 3 columns, "Transactions" spans 4, then Actions. `DataTable`'s flat column model has no colspan header groups.
- **Paired/heterogeneous rows** — each row is a receipt *side* + a transaction *side* (matched), or one side only (unmatched receipt/transaction), with 3 row `type`s.
- **Single-select for a match workflow** (`selectedUnmatchedTransaction`), not the multi-select-checkbox model `DataTable` provides.
- Sort is service-computed (`convertToDisplayRows(result, sort)`).

Forcing `DataTable` here would mean colspan support + row-type-switching cells + a different selection model — it'd make the shell's interface leakier for little gain. RF-03 scoped to the 3 flat-list pages for exactly this reason. Reconciliation's real cleanup is a different item (RF-10: it does UI display-massaging in the *service* — `convertToDisplayRows`/`sortDisplayRows` belong in a presenter). So: leave it out of the `DataTable` sweep.

---

## Now, transactions

Key facts from reading it: no selection today; its "bulk delete" is **filter-based** ("Delete Filtered (N)"), not selection-based; sort is server-side; edit is an inline **Edit button** (no row-click); `excluded` rows are dimmed. Per your earlier decisions, transactions gets **selection (multi-select, consistent)** and **row-click-to-edit** (removing the Edit button), while keeping its existing Delete-Filtered button as-is. Honest answer: **No — it's now inconsistent with receipts**, which is the only other page with a delete-selected. Ironically, the transactions layout you *had* before this last change matched receipts; moving it to the filter row diverged them.

## Receipts vs transactions (both delete-selected)

| | **Receipts** | **Transactions (now)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Placement** | Floating bar **above the table** | **Filter action row** (next to Apply/Clear Filters) |
| **Visibility** | Appears **only when rows are selected** | **Always visible, greyed** until selected |
| **Confirmation** | In-page **confirm dialog** (`showDeleteConfirm`) | Native `confirm()` |
| **Label** | "Delete N Selected" | "Delete Selected (N)" |

So three real differences: placement, visibility, and the confirmation mechanism.

(For completeness: **expenses** has selection checkboxes but *no* delete-selected at all — a third state.)

## Recommendation

Pick one standard and I'll align the others. Two directions:

- **A — adopt the new transactions pattern everywhere** (filter-row buttons, always-visible-greyed): update receipts to match, and give expenses the same. Stable layout, delete affordance always discoverable.
- **B — adopt the receipts pattern everywhere** (contextual bar above the table, shown only when selected): revert transactions back to that. More prominent/Gmail-like, but the layout shifts when it appears.

I'd lean **A**, since it's the behavior you just deliberately chose, and "always-visible-but-disabled" is more discoverable than a bar that only appears after you've already figured out selection. If we go A, I'd also standardize the confirmation — either keep native `confirm()` on both (simplest) or move transactions to the same in-page dialog receipts uses (nicer, more work).

All consistent now. Build clean, and **zero lint introduced** (expenses 8→7, receipts 13→12, transactions 16 — the removals even reduced two). Version 0.30.

## Delete-selected is now identical across all three pages

Same pattern everywhere — **in the filter action row, always visible, greyed/disabled until rows are selected**, `Delete Selected (N)` with a live count, **native `confirm()`**, optimistic update + rollback:

| Page | What it deletes | Confirm copy |
|---|---|---|
| **Transactions** | selected transactions (`deleteByIds`) | "Delete N selected transaction(s)?" |
| **Receipts** | selected receipts (`bulkDeleteReceipts`) | "…removes the record and the stored file." |
| **Expenses** | the **underlying receipts** (expense = receipt, 1:1) | "…removes the underlying receipt and its stored file." |

What changed this round:
- **Receipts:** removed the floating blue bar and the custom in-page confirm **dialog** (`showDeleteConfirm`/`confirmBulkDelete`/`executeBulkDelete`); collapsed to one `deleteSelected()` with native confirm, buttons moved into the filter row.
- **Expenses:** its selection was dead — now wired to a real `deleteSelected()` that bulk-deletes the underlying receipts, with a confirm that plainly says it removes the receipt + file.
- **Transactions:** the reference pattern, unchanged.

**Verified:** `svelte-check` **112** (baseline, zero new), suite **1600 green**, build clean. No introspection tests referenced the removed receipts dialog.

Two notes:
- The orphaned `tests/bulk-receipt-operations.spec.ts` (a Playwright spec that sits outside the test dir and never runs) still references the old receipts confirm dialog — it's now stale. It didn't run before either; flagging in case you ever un-orphan it.
- `deleteByIds`/`bulkDeleteReceipts` bulk deletes aren't unit-tested (singleton services, no harness — RF-07). Please exercise all three in the browser: nothing selected → Delete greyed; select some → count updates, delete removes exactly those and resets.

Please review + commit.
